person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: ONE WORD, DEFINED FIVE WAYS BY FIVE DISCIPLINES AT THE SAME TABLE - psychiatry, clinical psychology, developmental science, anthropology and neuroendocrinology each state a definition of `resilience` for their own unit of analysis, and the paper prints the disagreement instead of resolving it
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: how do we define resilience - and whether a field ought to agree on one definition at all, or carefully define several and say which is in use
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: four author-attributed definitions of one construct printed side by side, a decidable case on which they give opposite answers, and a named triad of definitional failure modes
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: critique
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: a construct that grew across five decades in engineering, ecology, development, psychiatry and anthropology, whose colloquial sense runs alongside its technical ones and whose scope changes with the unit of analysis
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: a recorded plenary panel - one chair putting four questions to four researchers, published as dialogue with the objections in place, not as a consensus statement
span.term: a recorded plenary panel - one chair putting four questions to four researchers, published as dialogue with the objections in place, not as a consensus statement
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: **FOUR DEFINITIONS OF ONE WORD, IN ONE SENTENCE, EACH WITH A NAMED AUTHOR AT THE SAME TABLE**: `Proposed definitions included A STABLE TRAJECTORY OF HEALTHY FUNCTIONING after a highly adverse event; A CONSCIOUS EFFORT TO MOVE FORWARD in an insightful and integrated positive manner ...; THE CAPACITY OF A DYNAMIC SYSTEM TO ADAPT SUCCESSFULLY to disturbances that threaten the viability, function, and development of that system; and A PROCESS TO HARNESS RESOURCES in order to sustain well-being.` The corpus holds committees that VOTE on a definition and reviews that COUNT them. **This is the first where the disagreement itself is the output**
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: **AND THE DEFINITIONS DISAGREE ON A DECIDABLE CASE, WHICH THE PAPER PRINTS AND DOES NOT ANSWER**: `should we classify a trauma survivor as resilient IF THAT PERSON DEVELOPS CHRONIC SYMPTOMS OF PTSD BUT ALSO FUNCTIONS AT A HIGH LEVEL, because they have succeeded in seeking out and using ample personal, material and social resources?` One patient, two published definitions, opposite verdicts - the COMPAS shape, for a construct rather than a metric
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: AND THE CHALLENGE IS MADE TO THE AUTHOR'S FACE AND PRINTED: `Dr. Bonanno, I'm very intrigued by your definition of resilience, BUT I DON'T KNOW WHETHER THE TRAJECTORY OF RESILIENCE YOU DESCRIBE ALLOWS RESILIENCE TO CO-OCCUR WITH PTSD or other illnesses ... MY OWN VIEW IS THAT TRAUMA SURVIVORS WHO DEVELOP PTSD MAY BE JUST AS RESILIENT as trauma survivors who don't develop PTSD.` A definitional objection with a name on each side of it
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: **AND THE PANEL REJECTS THE GOAL OF ONE DEFINITION, IN SO MANY WORDS**: `I don't think that THE GOAL IS TO COME UP WITH ONE DEFINITION for resilience ... WE SHOULD ABSOLUTELY NOT RESTRICT THE FIELD BY TETHERING IT TO ONE PERSON'S CONCEPTION ... So IT DOESN'T REALLY MATTER IF WE HAVE DIFFERENT DEFINITIONS of resilience. IT MATTERS THAT WE CONTINUE TO HAVE A CONVERSATION.` Against every other definitional body in this corpus, which exists to stop exactly that
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: AND THE STRONGEST STATEMENT OF THE PROBLEM COMES FROM ONE OF THE DEFINERS: `I'VE ARGUED RECENTLY THAT THE WORD RESILIENCE IS ALMOST USELESS AS A SINGLE WORD and that IT REALLY ONLY MAKES SENSE IF WE QUALIFY IT ... We introduced the phrases `MINIMAL-IMPACT RESILIENCE` and `EMERGENT RESILIENCE` as two forms of resilience but I THINK THERE ARE POTENTIALLY OTHER FORMS.` The remedy proposed is not a better definition but a **required modifier**
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: **AND A DEFINER NAMES THE SUB-TERMS HER OWN DEFINITION LEAVES UNDEFINED, IN THE SENTENCE AFTER GIVING IT**: `There are many issues we have to deal with when we take a broad definition like this one. AS A SCIENTIST, I HAVE TO DEFINE WHAT I MEAN BY `CAPACITY.` WHAT DOES IT MEAN TO ADAPT SUCCESSFULLY? I WANT TO BE ABLE TO MEASURE IT.` The definer auditing her own definition for undefined terms, unprompted
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: AND THE BREADTH IS A DESIGN GOAL, NOT AN ACCIDENT: `I AM LOOKING FOR A BROAD CONCEPTUAL DEFINITION of resilience that is SCALABLE ACROSS DIFFERENT DISCIPLINES AND LEVELS OF ANALYSIS ... you can use across system levels, FROM A MOLECULAR LEVEL TO THE LEVELS OF HUMAN BEHAVIOR in family, community or even societal contexts.` Scalability as a stated criterion for a definition - and the price of it is named two sentences later
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: AND A NAMED DISTINCTION INSIDE THE NON-PATHOLOGICAL GROUP: `we began to make a DISTINCTION in the non-PTSD group between RESISTANCE (survivors who did not develop psychopathology) and RECOVERY (survivors who did develop PTSD ... but who no longer had those symptoms) ... RESISTANCE depicted as NEVER DEVELOPING SYMPTOMS to adversity IS NOT THE SAME THING AT ALL as having symptoms and BOUNCING BACK.` Two things a single word had been covering, split and named
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: **AND THE DEFINITION CHANGES WHEN THE BEARER CHANGES - STATED WITH A WATCH**: `The watch was described as having the ability to `TAKE A LICKING AND KEEP ON TICKING.` So, FOR AN INANIMATE OBJECT, THE QUALITY OF NEVER BREAKING despite exposure IS A GOOD DEFINITION, BUT FOR A PERSON, perhaps it is better to conceptualize resilience as A PROCESS OF MOVING FORWARD and not returning back. WHEN A WATCH IS DROPPED, IT DOESN'T IMPROVE.` The clearest statement of unit-dependence I have read: the same word needs a different definition because **people can end up better than they started and objects cannot**
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: AND A PUBLISHED TRIAD OF DEFINITIONAL FAILURE MODES: `let us avoid what I call the three `DEADLY SINS OF RESILIENCE RESEARCH`. One ... is TO BE CONCEPTUALLY HAZY with respect to how we articulate resilience in settings that are different from our own. A second ... is TO BE EMPIRICALLY LIGHT ... And the third sin is TO BE METHODOLOGICALLY LAME with respect to how we measure resilience.` A controlled vocabulary of what goes wrong with a construct, named by an anthropologist
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: AND THE COLLOQUIAL SENSE IS NAMED AS THE SOURCE OF THE TROUBLE: `resilience, LIKE TRAUMA, IS ONE OF THOSE WORDS THAT HAS COLLOQUIAL MEANING. During general discourse, people talk about trauma and resilience IN VERY LOOSE TERMS. But when trauma researchers talk about trauma THEY HAVE SPECIFIC DEFINITIONS IN MIND. AND AS A FIELD WE STRUGGLE WITH THESE DEFINITIONS.` The technical term and the everyday word share a spelling and the field pays for it
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: AND THE UNRESOLVED CHOICE IS PRINTED AS A CHOICE, NOT SETTLED: `ON THE ONE HAND, the goal MAY NOT BE TO AGREE ON ONE DEFINITION of resilience, but rather TO CAREFULLY DEFINE VARIOUS TYPES of resilience depending on context. ON THE OTHER HAND, in order to establish A SINGLE BROADER, BUT NEVERTHELESS USEFUL, DEFINITION ... it will be essential TO COLLABORATE WITH EXPERTS WHO STUDY ENGINEERING, ECOLOGICAL, BIOLOGICAL, INDIVIDUAL, FAMILY, ORGANIZATIONAL AND CULTURAL RESILIENCE.` Both horns, neither taken, in the paper's own summary
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: **A COMPARISON GROUP THAT COULD NOT BE CONSTRUCTED, AND THE ONE AVAILABLE CONTROL WAS VISIBLY CONFOUNDED**: `When people asked us if we had a comparison group, WE COULD FIND ONLY ONE PERSON in our region of the United States who represented a reasonable comparison, because he left Cambodia just before the killings began. THAT INDIVIDUAL WAS A FOOT TALLER than any other person in our sample, likely due to the advantages in nutrition and protein intake he experienced. In other words, THE COMPARISON GROUP DID NOT MAKE IT OUT OF THE `KILLING FIELDS`.` Selection on survival removes the control arm, and the single survivor of the control condition **wears the confound at a foot of height**
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: AND NO DETERMINANT EXPLAINS MUCH: `If we measure many different predictors, we find that NO ONE PREDICTOR ACCOUNTS FOR MUCH VARIANCE ... NO SINGLE DEMOGRAPHIC, PERSONALITY OR BIOLOGICAL FACTOR has been shown to predict or enhance resilience BY MORE THAN A SMALL DEGREE.` A construct with four definitions and no strong predictor under any of them
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: AND A PROTECTIVE FACTOR THAT PRODUCES A BAD OUTCOME: `research on youth who become involved in POLITICAL VIOLENCE in Middle-Eastern conflict-prone areas indicates that THEY BECOME ENGAGED AT LEAST PARTLY BECAUSE IT GIVES THEM A SENSE OF MASTERY AND INVOLVEMENT` - offered against her own `favourite` adaptive system. The mechanism is protective; whether the outcome counts as resilience depends entirely on who is naming the adaptive criterion
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: AND THE FIELD'S STARTING DEFINITION IS REJECTED ON THE FIRST PAGE: `The American Psychological Association defines resilience as `THE PROCESS OF ADAPTING WELL IN THE FACE OF ADVERSITY, TRAUMA, TRAGEDY, THREATS OR EVEN SIGNIFICANT SOURCES OF STRESS.` While this definition is useful, IT DOES NOT REFLECT THE COMPLEX NATURE OF RESILIENCE.` The most-cited professional definition, set aside by the chair before the panel speaks
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: a comparison group of Cambodians who did not live through the Khmer Rouge period, sought for a study of refugee resilience in Minnesota
span.note: eliminates: nothing - it could not be assembled. One candidate existed in the region, and he was A FOOT TALLER than anyone in the sample from better nutrition · outcome: failed
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: requiring operational definitions and empirically driven criteria before calling a response resilient, rather than the colloquial sense of the word
span.note: eliminates: the loose everyday sense of `resilience` leaking into the technical claim · outcome: partial

span.label: checking a proposed protective factor against outcomes nobody wants - agency and mastery motivation tested against youth engagement in political violence
span.note: eliminates: the assumption that an adaptive SYSTEM produces an adaptive OUTCOME · outcome: failed

span.label: `resilience` (Bonanno, clinical psychology) - A STABLE TRAJECTORY OF HEALTHY FUNCTIONING after a highly adverse event; explicitly `NOT SIMPLY THE ABSENCE OF PSYCHOPATHOLOGY`, and distinct from other non-pathological patterns
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: `resilience` (Yehuda, neuroendocrinology/psychiatry) - A REINTEGRATION OF SELF including a conscious effort to MOVE FORWARD in an insightful integrated positive manner; may co-occur with severe PTSD, and is `an active decision, LIKE SOBRIETY, that must be frequently reconfirmed`
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: `resilience` (Masten, developmental science) - THE CAPACITY OF A DYNAMIC SYSTEM TO ADAPT SUCCESSFULLY to disturbances that threaten its viability, function or development; chosen to be SCALABLE from the molecular to the societal
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: `resilience` (Panter-Brick, anthropology) - A PROCESS TO HARNESS RESOURCES IN ORDER TO SUSTAIN WELL-BEING; `process` because it is not an attribute or a capacity, and `well-being` because it is more than the absence of pathology
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: `resistance` vs `recovery` - never developing symptoms, against developing them and no longer having them: `NOT THE SAME THING AT ALL`
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: `resilience` - THE CATEGORY QUESTION, ORTHOGONAL TO WHOSE DEFINITION YOU TAKE: the paper says a definer must first specify whether the word names A TRAIT, A PROCESS, OR AN OUTCOME. This record already carries four disciplinary definitions (Bonanno, Yehuda, Masten, Panter-Brick); this axis cuts ACROSS all four, because two people can pick the same definition and still disagree about what KIND of thing it names. The paper also names the failure that follows - treating it as present or absent.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: `resilience` - THE LEVEL-OF-ANALYSIS AXIS, AGREED BY THE PANEL RATHER THAN DISPUTED: the term `MAY BE DEFINED DIFFERENTLY in the context of individuals, families, organizations, societies, and cultures`. A SECOND ORTHOGONAL AXIS - a trait-reading at the individual level and a process-reading at the societal level are two independent choices, so the four named definitions do not exhaust the space they sit in. Note this one is CONSENSUS, not disagreement: the panel agrees the term is level-relative.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: critiques → the American Psychological Association's definition of resilience - `While this definition is useful, IT DOES NOT REFLECT THE COMPLEX NATURE OF RESILIENCE`
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: critiques → the use of `resilience` unqualified - `THE WORD RESILIENCE IS ALMOST USELESS AS A SINGLE WORD and ... it really only makes sense IF WE QUALIFY IT`
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: extends → the binary reading of resilience as present-or-absent - replaced by a continuum that `may be present to differing degrees ACROSS MULTIPLE DOMAINS OF LIFE`, so one person may be resilient at work and not at home
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: resilience —operationalised-as→ stable trajectory of healthy functioning
span.note: the relation itself is separately evidenced · strength of the relation: 0.95 — `Quotation withheld` This is the only one of the four definitions in the paper that names a measurable object - and its author is the one who says the word is `ALMOST USELESS AS A SINGLE WORD`. The other three define a CAPACITY, a PROCESS and a CONSCIOUS EFFORT, none of which the paper operationalises
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: resilience trajectory —distinct-from→ absence of psychopathology
span.note: the relation itself is separately evidenced · strength of the relation: 0.95 — `Quotation withheld.` The third category is the load-bearing part: a response can be neither ill nor resilient, which most binary readings of the word cannot say
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: resilience —distinct-from→ absence of pathology
span.note: the relation itself is separately evidenced · strength of the relation: 0.95 — `And I like the expression `SUSTAINED WELL-BEING` BECAUSE RESILIENCE INVOLVES MORE THAN JUST A NARROW DEFINITION OF HEALTH OR THE ABSENCE OF PATHOLOGY.` Two panellists from two disciplines deny the same equation independently, in different words, for different reasons - and neither cites the other doing it
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: resistance —distinct-from→ recovery
span.note: the relation itself is separately evidenced · strength of the relation: 0.95 — `we began to make A DISTINCTION in the non-PTSD group between RESISTANCE (e.g., survivors who DID NOT DEVELOP psychopathology) and RECOVERY (e.g., survivors who DID develop PTSD, or other symptoms, BUT WHO NO LONGER HAD THOSE SYMPTOMS) ... RESISTANCE depicted as never developing symptoms IS NOT THE SAME THING AT ALL as having symptoms and BOUNCING BACK.` The split is what leads Yehuda to her own definition, in which resilience may co-occur with PTSD
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: bicycle helmets —causes→ accidents
span.note: the relation itself is separately evidenced · strength of the relation: 0.85 — `if we look at the literature on human factors, we see that interventions like BICYCLE HELMETS, OR SEAT BELTS, WHICH MAKE PEOPLE SAFER ACTUALLY TEND TO INCREASE ACCIDENTS. That's because people feel safer so they become less cautious.` Reported from another literature, not measured here - hence weight 0.85 - and used to make a definitional point: `we have to make sure that WE ARE NOT UNDERMINING PEOPLE'S NATURAL RESILIENCE`, which only bites if resilience is a BASELINE rather than a deficit to be filled
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: `A STABLE TRAJECTORY OF HEALTHY FUNCTIONING after a highly adverse event; A CONSCIOUS EFFORT TO MOVE FORWARD ...; THE CAPACITY OF A DYNAMIC SYSTEM TO ADAPT SUCCESSFULLY to disturbances that threaten the viability, function, and development of that system; and A PROCESS TO HARNESS RESOURCES in order to sustain well-being`. **THE SENTENCE THAT CARRIES ALL FOUR NEVER USES THE WORD ITSELF** - it sits under the section heading `How do we define resilience?`, so the term is attested here by `definitions`, not by `resilience`

span.label: `CONCEPTUALLY HAZY` (how it is articulated in unfamiliar settings), `EMPIRICALLY LIGHT` (evidence across a broad range of contexts), `METHODOLOGICALLY LAME` (how it is measured where cultural goals are less familiar). Three named failure modes, each attached to a different stage of getting from a word to a number

span.label: `In defining resilience, IT IS IMPORTANT TO SPECIFY WHETHER RESILIENCE IS BEING VIEWED AS A TRAIT, A PROCESS, OR AN OUTCOME` - three incompatible ontological readings of one word, and the paper says which you pick must be declared
